evals.prompt: I have a new product idea: let users save and restore named layouts. The behavior is still fuzzy. Help me shape it and create the right Linear work.
evals.expected_output: Stops at an Alignment Profile Gate, proposes one exact harness/model/reasoning combination, waits for confirmation, and only then creates the Task and terminal. After a verified launch it hands the conversation to the Alignment terminal.
expectations: Proposes exactly one Alignment harness/model/reasoning tuple
Waits for explicit user confirmation before any task-create or terminal creation
Creates the Alignment Task before launching the terminal
Inlines the complete initial request in the Task instead of asking the user to repeat it
Tells the user to switch to the named Alignment terminal

evals.prompt: The mute button is visibly on but audio still plays. Repro and expected behavior are already precise; make this ready for an agent.
evals.expected_output: Uses the adaptive bounded-bug path: focused clarification plus /to-tickets without forcing /to-spec, then verifies the resulting Linear tickets by readback.
expectations: Does not require /to-spec for this single bounded bug
Recommends /to-tickets as the next user-invoked step
Verifies the final ticket state by reading Linear back rather than trusting prose

evals.prompt: Start implementing ITEM-101 and ITEM-102 with Orca. Pick whatever models you think are best and get going.
evals.expected_output: Stops at the Execution Profile Gate, proposes role-specific profiles plus the parallel limit and validation commands, and waits for confirmation before generating a handoff or launching a Coordinator.
expectations: Proposes profiles for Coordinator, Worker, Reviewer, Integration Worker, and Integration Reviewer
Worker and Reviewer come from different model families
Proposes a cheaper model for the orchestration-only Coordinator than for the Worker
Checks provider headroom once and skips a provider whose window is in deficit
Resolves fast-tier and full-suite commands and records their source
Waits for explicit confirmation before generating the handoff
Freezes confirmed values in a Wave Manifest saved beside the handoff

evals.prompt: The ITEM-101 reviewer requested changes. Keep the existing agents' context and have the original worker fix it, then let the same reviewer check the delta.
evals.expected_output: Retains and re-dispatches both terminals in the same Issue Worktree with fresh lifecycle envelopes but delta-only Task bodies.
expectations: Re-dispatches the original Worker terminal, then the original Reviewer terminal
Sends a fresh lifecycle envelope with new Task/Dispatch IDs
Delta Task carries changed commits, active findings, acceptance changes, and invalidations only
Does not repeat or reload stable role, profile, Orca, or project-doc context
Keeps review outcome separate from verdict and releases neither terminal

evals.prompt: PROJECT-102 was accepted, but merging it into master conflicts with changes from another accepted ticket. Finish integration safely.
evals.expected_output: Runs a non-mutating preflight, and because content conflicts exist creates a dedicated Integration Worktree with an Integration Worker and fresh Integration Reviewer before advancing main.
expectations: Runs a non-mutating merge preflight before creating any worktree
Creates a dedicated Integration Worktree only because conflicts exist
Assigns resolving-merge-conflicts to the Integration Worker
Requires a fresh Integration Reviewer verdict before main advances
Confirms main has not advanced immediately before advancing it

evals.prompt: You are the newly launched Alignment Agent. Main already handed you complete feedback about auto-hiding a top toolbar plus several settings-panel behavior changes. Begin the alignment session.
evals.expected_output: Runs the runtime profile probe first, then makes a first human-facing response with the attestation, a feedback summary, and exactly one recommended slash command.
expectations: First action is the harness-native profile probe
First visible response shows the exact profile attestation
Summarizes the received feedback points
Recommends exactly one next slash skill with its exact command
Does no broad repository or Linear exploration before that response

evals.prompt: Before launching Alignment, find a good harness/model/thinking combination and confirm it with me. Keep the discovery cheap.
evals.expected_output: Queries the current profile once, validates only the proposed candidate, proposes a single tuple, and stops for confirmation.
expectations: Reads the current PI_PROVIDER/PI_MODEL/PI_REASONING_LEVEL in one call
Validates only the one proposed candidate
Does not enumerate all models, accounts, agents, or quotas
Creates no Task and no terminal

evals.prompt: The Alignment Agent sent a complete verified ticket manifest. Main considers alignment finished. Clean up the Alignment Agent.
evals.expected_output: Processes the Delivery, releases the settled Alignment terminal immediately, acknowledges once, and retains nothing for reuse.
expectations: Calls worker-release before acknowledging the Delivery
Acknowledges the whole Delivery exactly once
Does not retain or plan to re-dispatch the Alignment terminal
Does not ask for extra user approval to close it

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. The ITEM-104 implementation Worker just reported a clean committed head and passing tests. Start code review.
evals.expected_output: Performs metadata-only checks, retains the Worker, and dispatches a fresh read-only Reviewer in the same Issue Worktree.
expectations: Checks lifecycle IDs, commit existence, exact HEAD, clean status, and base ancestry
Does not run git diff, read changed files, load code-review, or rerun tests for a verdict
Retains the Worker terminal
Dispatches a fresh Reviewer with the confirmed Reviewer profile in the same worktree
Issues no ACCEPT of its own

evals.prompt: ITEM-105 is accepted. Main has advanced since its base, but a non-mutating merge preflight shows no content conflicts. Integrate it without unnecessary workspace setup.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the existing Issue Worktree for the mechanical candidate, validates there, and fast-forwards main only after tree equivalence.
expectations: Creates no dedicated Integration Worktree
Takes the worktree mutation lock before staging, confirming Dispatches are settled and terminals idle
Materializes the mechanical candidate with current main as first parent
Validates the combined state in the Issue Worktree
Advances main only after an unchanged main head and tree equivalence

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator and your profile matches the manifest. Create your Run and tell Main you are ready.
evals.expected_output: Creates the Run, then reports readiness through a real Orca message type carrying the coordinator_ready subject.
expectations: Sends readiness with a valid --type value from Orca's enum
Carries coordinator_ready as the subject rather than as the type
Addresses the Main Run explicitly with --to run:<mainRun>
Includes the Coordinator Run ID and accepted manifest version

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. Your 15-minute wait for ITEM-107's worker just timed out with no messages at all, and its last heartbeat was two cadences ago. Handle it.
evals.expected_output: Treats silence as a stall and climbs the ladder instead of waiting again or assuming completion.
expectations: Inspects the Dispatch with worker-show and one bounded worker-read
Escalates to worker-stop, or worker-abandon when the process cannot be proven stopped
Relaunches with worker-start --retry-of carrying the full role Task and durable artifacts
Marks the ticket blocked and escalates to Main after two failed relaunches

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. ITEM-108 has now had two focused re-reviews plus a clean-room review, and the fresh reviewer still returns REQUEST_CHANGES. What now?
evals.expected_output: Ends the fix loop, marks the ticket blocked, and escalates with both review artifacts rather than dispatching another fix.
expectations: Dispatches no further fix pass
Reports the ticket outcome as blocked with a reason
Escalates to Main with both review artifacts and the surviving findings
Preserves commits, worktree, and review artifacts

evals.prompt: Deliver GH-42 and GH-43 through the Orca loop. This repo tracks work in GitHub Issues, as docs/agents/issue-tracker.md says.
evals.expected_output: Stops at the tracker check: the loop needs Linear through orca linear, so it reports the mismatch instead of running Linear operations or improvising a GitHub path.
expectations: Detects that the configured tracker is not Linear through orca linear
Stops before creating a handoff, Coordinator, or worktree
Explains the Alignment-to-Execution mismatch to the user
Offers the Linear tracker seed template as the fix

evals.prompt: Kick off delivery for PROJECT-201. There is no docs/agents directory in this repo at all.
evals.expected_output: Names the missing tracker configuration, points at /setup-matt-pocock-skills, and resolves validation commands from the repository itself rather than assuming absent documents.
expectations: Tells the user to run /setup-matt-pocock-skills for the missing tracker configuration
Does not treat a missing domain document as an error
Derives fast-tier and full-suite commands from repository scripts or asks once
Records the resolved commands and their source in the Wave Manifest

evals.prompt: Stop the ITEM-110 wave, I changed my mind about the approach.
evals.expected_output: Runs the abort path: stops live Dispatches, leaves main and Linear lifecycle untouched, preserves committed work, and reports where each ticket stopped.
expectations: Sends the stop instruction to the Coordinator Run and waits for acknowledgement
Stops live Dispatches with worker-stop or worker-abandon
Leaves main unchanged and posts no Linear completion comment or labels
Reports each affected ticket as abandoned with the user-abort reason and the retained resources

evals.prompt: Just this one ticket, ITEM-111, it is a two-line fix. Skip the ceremony and do it yourself.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the single Coordinator path: Main still gates profiles and hands delivery off instead of implementing, reviewing, or integrating in the Main session.
expectations: Main does not implement, review, or integrate the change itself
Runs the Execution Profile Gate for the single ticket
Hands delivery to a Coordinator with a Wave Manifest
Keeps inner Worker and Reviewer mail in the Coordinator Run

evals.prompt: For the ITEM-120 wave just use one model everywhere, whatever you are running right now. Simpler that way.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the Worker and Reviewer must differ in family and asks for a decision instead of silently accepting one model for both.
expectations: Names the correlated-blind-spot reason for cross-family review
Proposes a different family for the Reviewer than the Worker
Proceeds with one family only after an explicit user decision recorded in the manifest
Still proposes a cheaper Coordinator profile rather than reusing the premium one everywhere

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator for a five-ticket wave. The manifest gives two worker tuples and two reviewer tuples. Assign agents for the first three tickets.
evals.expected_output: Assigns a cross-family pair per ticket from the pools, balances by headroom and round-robin within maxConcurrent, pins each pair to its ticket, and records the assignment.
expectations: Each ticket gets one worker entry and one reviewer entry of different families
Balances across pool entries instead of sending every ticket to one entry
Respects each entry's maxConcurrent limit
Pins the pair so fix passes and re-reviews reuse the same entries
Records the assigned entry ids per ticket for the wave report

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. ITEM-130's pinned worker tuple now fails to launch because that provider's window is exhausted. The manifest's worker pool has another confirmed tuple.
evals.expected_output: Fails over to the other confirmed pool entry, keeps the family constraint, and needs no new user confirmation; a substitute outside the pool would require one.
expectations: Fails over to another entry inside the confirmed pool
Keeps the reviewer's family different from the substituted worker's family
Does not ask for new confirmation for an in-pool substitution
Records the substitution and the provider error
Reports profile_mismatch and waits if only an out-of-pool substitute would work

evals.prompt: Set up a delivery wave for ORCA-55 on this machine. There is no pi and no codexbar installed here, only Orca and a logged-in Codex account.
evals.expected_output: Degrades discovery to the sources that exist, asks the user for what none of them can answer, and records that headroom is unknown rather than assuming it is unlimited.
expectations: Probes tool availability once instead of assuming pi or codexbar
Uses Orca-native sources such as orca account list for auth readiness
Takes a one-shot smoke flag from the harness's own --help instead of reaching for pi
Asks the user for model ids or families it cannot discover
Records headroom as unknown in the manifest instead of assuming headroom
Still enforces different Worker and Reviewer families

evals.prompt: You are the Alignment Agent. The layouts feature went through /grill-with-docs and /to-spec, and /to-tickets just published PROJECT-201 through PROJECT-204. Finish the alignment session.
evals.expected_output: Labels each executable ticket with a complexity tier from the project vocabulary, verifies the label strings exist in the team, and reports complexity per ticket in the completion payload.
expectations: Reads the complexity vocabulary and repo anchors from docs/agents/agent-profiles.md
Verifies the three label strings exist with orca linear team labels before applying them
Labels executable tickets only, not the spec parent
Assigns each tier by what that ticket's own decision costs, not by diff size
Does not inflate tiers because the feature was grilled; settled decisions yield simple tickets
Treats a ticket that changes a contract other modules depend on as complex even when its diff is small
Reports complexity per ticket in the worker_done payload
Continues and names the missing vocabulary instead of blocking when a label does not exist

evals.prompt: Deliver PROJECT-201 and PROJECT-202. We already picked our usual models for this repo weeks ago.
evals.expected_output: Finds the stored profile file, revalidates it cheaply, and asks for a one-word confirmation instead of re-running discovery.
expectations: Reads docs/agents/agent-profiles.md before any discovery command
Checks host match, age against maxAgeDays, and one bounded auth check per entry it will launch
Reads headroom fresh rather than trusting a stored value
Proposes the stored pools as a one-line summary and takes a one-word confirmation
Falls back to full discovery and offers to update the file when a check fails

evals.prompt: You are the Coordinator. ITEM-140 is labelled complex and ITEM-141 is simple. The worker pool has one premium entry trusted with standard and complex, and one cheap entry trusted with simple and standard.
evals.expected_output: Routes the complex ticket to the premium entry and the simple one to the cheap entry, keeping cross-family review for both.
expectations: Sends the complex ticket to the entry whose tiers include complex
Does not consume the premium entry for the simple ticket
Keeps each ticket's reviewer family different from its worker family
Plans a full-suite rerun for the complex ticket's fix passes
Records both assignments with their complexity for the wave report

evals.prompt: I want to use my z.ai GLM models for the reviewer pool. pi auth check says that provider is not ready, but I use it every day and it works fine.
evals.expected_output: Does not drop the provider on the probe result: it smoke-tests the model with one real call, and either proposes it on that evidence or quotes the provider error and asks the user to decide.
expectations: Does not discard the provider because the auth probe reported not ready
Runs one bounded non-interactive smoke call against the exact model
Judges the returned output rather than the exit status
Proposes the candidate when the smoke call answers, recording the smoke test as its evidence
Quotes the exact provider error and asks the user to decide when the call fails
Falls back to the user decision and a first-launch test when no CLI on the host can make a one-shot call
Records the user's vouch in the profile file so the question is not repeated every wave

evals.prompt: You are the Alignment Agent. Every one of the six tickets you just sliced from the notifications spec looks like it needs a structural decision. Finish the session.
evals.expected_output: Treats an all-design slice set as a signal about the alignment rather than labelling around it, and says so in the completion report.
expectations: Notices that nearly every slice landed in standard or complex
Reads it as unresolved structure pushed downstream or slices that are too wide
Checks that no executable ticket still carries an open question, which would need the needs-info role instead
Reports the observation so the user can choose to keep aligning or accept the tiers
Does not silently downgrade tiers to make the distribution look better
